chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Mufaddal ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Zurara narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Abu Amr al-Jallab, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he said:
Islam began as something strange and will return as something strange as it began, so good news is for the strangers.
ai.seo_question: What does the hadith mean by Islam being 'strange' and who are the 'strangers'?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (as), highlights the cyclical nature of Islamic authenticity, where the core tenets remain distinct and often marginalized amidst societal conformity. It serves as a spiritual comfort to the 'Ghuraba' (strangers)—those who preserve the true Sunnah and Ahl al-Bayt's teachings in times of widespread deviation. The concept underscores the Shia emphasis on remaining faithful to the original message even when it contradicts the majority opinion or political power.
